subject.title: Text between tool calls leaks to messaging channels

question: For external channel sessions, should OpenClaw keep automatic bare-text source replies as the default while adding narrower final-only/internal-text guards, or should it move direct/group/channel source replies toward explicit message-tool-only delivery with a migration path?
rationale: Current docs and tests make automatic visible replies a compatibility contract, while the production reports show that the same default can leak internal assistant output into customer or team channels; the tradeoff is product/security policy, not just a code location choice.

options.title: Generic guard with compatibility plan
options.body: Preserve intentional automatic final replies where required, but suppress internal/pre-tool/inter-tool text through a generic delivery-boundary rule and document or migrate any changed defaults.

options.title: Explicit message-tool default
options.body: Make external source replies message-tool-only or final-only by default, accepting that existing bare-text reply deployments need migration, docs, and upgrade proof.

options.title: Opt-in mitigations only
options.body: Land only opt-in safeguards such as final-tag or verbose-off suppression, which reduces urgent pain for configured users but leaves the default leak class open.

recommendation.title: Generic guard with compatibility plan
recommendation.body: Preserve intentional automatic final replies where required, but suppress internal/pre-tool/inter-tool text through a generic delivery-boundary rule and document or migrate any changed defaults.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent visible-reply default history and docs tie this compatibility decision most closely to the current source-reply policy surface.
